faq.a: Rauf is associated with the Arabic form رَؤُوف, whose core sense is rauf; compassionate, kind.

faq.q: What is the origin of Rauf?
faq.a: Rauf is associated with Arabic. Rauf is Arabic رَؤُوف (Raʾūf), meaning 'compassionate, kind'.
Yes — the underlying form رَؤُوف is Arabic.
Rauf can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Rauf should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ر أ ف is Quranic (compassion), but Raʾūf is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Rauf mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Rauf is rendered رؤف and carries the sense رؤف، مہربان.

faq.q: What does Rauf mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Rauf is rendered رئوف and carries the sense رئوف، مهربان.
A romanized syllable approximation is rauf. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Rauf?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Rauf, rauf. Script forms are رؤف, رؤوف, رئوف, رَؤُوف, रऊफ़.

faq.q: Is Rauf a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
